basisLabels: Political power, institutions and political thought
courseTraceability.rationale: Law, Society & Justice offers legal, social and normative perspectives on how societies and their institutions -- including public and international law -- are governed. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political power, institutions and political thought”.

basisLabels: Political power, institutions and political thought
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Political Philosophy examines the views of influential Western thinkers on political authority, the state and society. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political power, institutions and political thought”.

basisLabels: Political power, institutions and political thought

basisLabels: Political economy and public governance
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Economics introduces the micro- and macroeconomic principles that underpin the study of global political economy. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political economy and public governance”.

basisLabels: Empirical quantitative and qualitative political inquiry
courseTraceability.rationale: Research Methods & Statistics is the general introduction to research design, operationalisation, sampling, survey research and descriptive/inferential statistics, implementing quantitative political research, survey design and statistics for political science. It implements the explicit academic basis “Empirical quantitative and qualitative political inquiry”.

basisLabels: International relations, law and security
courseTraceability.rationale: Theory of International Relations gives a historical and contemporary grounding in International Relations and geopolitics, including the conflict and cooperation among states that the programme's own core studies. basisLabels: International relations, law and security

basisLabels: Political economy and public governance

basisLabels: International relations, law and security

notes.text: UCR offers broader political, legal, economic and empirical inquiry. It does not reproduce the two dedicated VU political research projects, the full political-methods sequence or the required final political-science thesis. The security option combines actual conflict, law, warfare and radicalisation inquiry; it is not equivalent specialist security training.

audience.programmeDescription: Global Politics studies political power, international conflict and cooperation, global governance, comparative regimes and political economy, with quantitative and qualitative research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The confirmed global politics and empirical-methods core supports two meaningful broader UCR responses, while the revised-cohort final-year theory and research culmination remains outside the assessed scope. UCR supplies sustained political/institutional and empirical study with the option-specific emphases shown. Dedicated VU projects and the final thesis are not reproduced; a complete external progression pathway is not certified.
